clue.text: Our colonel first to blush…

indicators.note: first tells us the colonel's letters lead, before the word our

parts.note: COL is the standard abbreviation for the army rank of colonel
taken as written

explanation.surface: An officer who reddens with embarrassment, the sentence trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To blush is to redden, to take on a flush of hue in the face.

clue.text: … man, good man, putting on uniform

indicators.note: putting on places the saint's letters ahead of the next piece, as if donning it

parts.note: ST, short for saint, is the crossword's usual good man
uniform in the sense of level or regular means even

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a decent fellow getting dressed in a uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Steven is a male first name, so it can stand for a man.

clue.text: Pub providing good garden range (to order)

indicators.note: arranged to order means the letters are rearranged into a new sequence

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub that offers a fine garden and a cooking range made to order.
explanation.walkthrough: The GEORGE AND DRAGON, named after England's patron saint and his legendary foe, is a very common English pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional English inn sign; many taverns carry this name.

clue.text: Footballers magazine

definitions.meaning: a famous north London football club
a magazine in the military sense is a store of arms and ammunition

explanation.surface: A football team and a periodical.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a London football club, and an arsenal is a weapons store, which is one sense of magazine.

clue.text: Where, to have fun underneath the arches?

definitions.text: Where, to have fun underneath the arches?

parts.words: Where, to have fun underneath the arches?
parts.note: a place for amusement, read as being beneath a covered row of arches, as a seaside gaming hall is

explanation.surface: Asking where one might enjoy oneself beneath railway arches, as in the old music-hall song.
explanation.walkthrough: An arcade is literally a row of arches, so the place of fun sits 'under arches'.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside hall of slot machines and games for entertainment, the word arcade meaning a covered arched passage.

clue.text: Plant cut back by everyone in retirement

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so the next piece follows on

parts.note: to prune is to cut back a shrub

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the word for everyone is read in reverse

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: A plant pruned by every gardener now enjoying their retirement.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-heal, a low-growing herb of the mint family, belongs to this genus.

clue.text: Mark of very little intelligence?

parts.note: seems to describe a sign of stupidity, but means a tiny dot carrying espionage information

explanation.surface: A sign that someone is rather dim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intelligence' means secret information, as in spying, not brainpower.
explanation.definitionFit: A photograph shrunk to the size of a full stop, used by spies to carry secret information.

clue.text: Wellington, for example, wrote of a different way

indicators.note: written in a different way means the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Duke of Wellington writing of some other route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wellington' looks like the Duke but is a rubber boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellington is a rubber boot, an example of something worn on the feet.

clue.text: Space on page to show profit made on a deal?

definitions.meaning: the blank border around printed text
the difference between cost and selling price

explanation.surface: A blank border on a page shown as the gain on a transaction.
explanation.definitionFit: The blank edge of a page and a trader's mark-up both go by this word.

clue.text: American Indian said to have very little money

indicators.note: said tells us we go by the way the people's name is pronounced

parts.note: a Sioux is a member of a Native American people

explanation.surface: A Native American reputed to be nearly penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: A sou was an old French coin of small value, hence a trifling sum.

clue.text: Exchange of views with opposite

definitions.meaning: talk, conversation, an archaic noun sense

explanation.surface: A discussion held with someone who takes the contrary view.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word once meant conversation, and it also means the reverse of a statement.

clue.text: Guard transported by rail

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so the next piece follows

parts.note: sent means dispatched or transported
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A guard dispatched on a train.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier posted to keep watch, a guard.

clue.text: Preserve from Granada -meal more varied?

indicators.note: varied means changed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jam bought in Spain, with more of the meal thrown in.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a citrus jam, and jam is a preserve.

clue.text: Fit tap that turns

indicators.note: turns means the letters of the word are moved around

parts.note: taken as written; the letters also running across tap that is a coincidence, as the setter signals rearranging

explanation.surface: A plumbing fitting: a tap that turns on.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt means suitable, fitting.

clue.text: Playing snooker in garden-shed?

definitions.meaning: what a gardener does at the bench, putting plants into containers of compost

explanation.surface: A game of snooker played inside the garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both sinking a ball in a pocket and planting seedlings in containers.

clue.text: Topple vase presented to public

indicators.note: presented to puts the vase's letters after the public piece

parts.note: overt means open, public
an urn is a vase

explanation.surface: Knocking over a vase that was being shown to the public.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn is to tip over, knock down.

clue.text: Bunfight in Boston?

parts.note: a bunfight is jokey British slang for a teatime gathering; the one in Boston was the 1773 protest of tea dumped into the harbour

explanation.surface: A squabble in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunfight' sounds like a brawl, but is British slang for a gathering with buns and tea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boston protest against tax on tea is known by this name, also a social gathering with cakes.

clue.text: For leisurely repentance, get tied up, thus

definitions.text: For leisurely repentance, get tied up, thus

parts.words: For leisurely repentance, get tied up, thus
parts.note: refers to the proverb 'marry quickly, repent at leisure', getting tied up meaning getting married

explanation.surface: Advice on how to bring about a slow regret: get bound up.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'Marry in haste, repent at leisure'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something hurriedly, which by the proverb leads to long regret.

clue.text: Well in the spring

parts.note: seems to mean healthy in springtime, but describes a mineral spring resort

explanation.surface: Feeling healthy when spring comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' means a water source, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: A resort with a mineral spring, where people take the waters.

clue.text: Perfect rural area of Greece

parts.note: a mountainous region of the Peloponnese, also the poets' ideal of pastoral bliss

explanation.surface: An idyllic patch of Greek countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A region of the Peloponnese that poets made the byword for an unspoilt pastoral paradise.

clue.text: Accommodation in base with soldiers, for example?

parts.note: a bed is a base or foundation, as a road bed
with means and
soldiers are strips of toast for dipping in a boiled egg, a British morning dish

explanation.surface: Lodgings at an army base among the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldiers' here are British toast fingers dipped in a soft-boiled egg, eaten in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A guesthouse offering a room for the night and a morning meal is a form of lodging.

clue.text: Defoe's day on the beach

parts.note: a weekday, which is also the name of the islander Robinson Crusoe meets on the shore in Defoe's novel

explanation.surface: A novelist enjoying a seaside outing.
explanation.walkthrough: Robinson Crusoe named his companion after the weekday on which they met; Crusoe first saw his footprint on the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a day of the week and the companion in Robinson Crusoe.

clue.text: Nurse about to marry in this country

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the nurse's letters go round the marriage word

parts.note: SEN was a State Enrolled Nurse in Britain
to wed is to marry

explanation.surface: A nurse about to marry in a particular country.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweden is a Scandinavian nation.

clue.text: A pie's turned over in layers

indicators.note: turned over means the whole string of letters is read back to front

parts.note: a tart is a pie, and the 's gives the plural form

explanation.surface: A layered pie that has been flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are beds of rock or levels, layers.

clue.text: Old records of principal American conductor

parts.note: arch as an adjective means chief, principal
Charles Ives was an American composer, here a conductor of music

explanation.surface: Historical documents of America's leading conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Archives are collections of historical documents.

clue.text: Son of Jacob to wander about

definitions.meaning: one of the twelve sons in Genesis, founder of a tribe of Israel

explanation.surface: A biblical son who likes to roam.
explanation.definitionFit: Gad is one of Jacob's sons in Genesis, and to gad about is to roam around.

clue.text: Greek with German fellow in cave

parts.note: Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A Greek and a German in a cave together.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small cave.

clue.text: Old ships at end of booked passage?

definitions.text: Old ships at end of booked passage?

parts.words: Old ships at end of booked passage?
parts.note: trading vessels of the East India Company; their passengers had booked a passage to the subcontinent and arrived there

explanation.surface: Ships waiting at the end of a voyage someone has booked.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue nods to E.M. Forster's novel A Passage to India.
explanation.definitionFit: Large merchant ships trading with the East under the East India Company.
